blocks.text: Interviews are one of the richest and most insidious sources: the interviewed person speaks firsthand, but chooses what to say and what to keep quiet, and the journalist chooses what to ask and what to publish. In this unit you learn the genres of the interview (printed, television, radio), the types of question and their purpose, the characteristics of fuṣḥā spoken (falling desires, filling words, self-corrections), the techniques by which an interviewee avoids a question and the way to report precisely what has been said and what has not been said. Four weeks, in parallel with the end of EGY-13 and the beginning of EGY-14.

Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. recognize the genres of the interview and their conventions (demand and answer, introduction, title);
2. classify questions (open, closed, in-depth, oriented) and understand what they are looking for;
3. follow the fuṣḥā talk of an interview, with its simplifications and its filling words;
4. recognize when an interviewee does not respond, and how he does so;
5. report an interview with the right verbs, including waste and non-answers ( ⁧رَفَضَ التَّعْلِيقَ⁩ , ⁧لَمْ يَسْتَبْعِدْ⁩ ).
